sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: S6-p75NTR-EGFP induced growth cone collapse in neurons upon proNGF administration, indistinguishable from untagged p75NTR constructs (L6); surface biotinylation and Alexa647 labelling confirmed cell-surface display (L8, L9). Function PRESERVED.
sites.rationale: L7 explicitly places the S6 tag 'between the signal peptide (SP) and cysteine-rich domains 1 to 4 (CRD1-4)', which in the canonical 427-aa sequence corresponds to the junction after residue 28 (last residue of the signal peptide, A) and before residue 29 (K, the mature N-terminus). No specific residue number is cited in the paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived: the SP/CRD1 boundary is the only extracellular N-terminal junction available. Python lookup confirms residue 28 = A and residue 29 = K, and the junction is 223 residues from the TM boundary (252), well above the 3-residue minimum. L6 confirms full functional preservation (growth cone collapse) and L8/L9 confirm surface display. Full-length membrane-anchored P75NTR constructs bearing 12-aa ACP/PCP-family tags (A1: GDSLDMLEWSLM; S6: GDSLSWLLRLLN) inserted immediately downstream of the signal peptide, between the SP cleavage site and CRD1 of the extracellular domain, expressed in SHSY5Y cells. S6-p75NTR-EGFP localises to the plasma membrane and the S6 tag is accessible to enzymatic biotinylation and Alexa647 conjugation on the cell surface.

sources.claim: The S6 tag is inserted between the signal peptide (SP) and cysteine-rich domains 1 to 4 (CRD1-4).

literature_notes: All nine ledger lines (L1–L9) from two papers (PMC4245215 and PMC6815156) describe the same single insertion event: ACP/PCP-family 12-aa tags (A1 and S6) placed immediately after the signal peptide of full-length membrane-anchored P75NTR/NGFR. No residue number is named in any clip, but the junction is uniquely determined by the SP/CRD1 boundary (after residue 28). No internal extracellular loop insertions, no C-terminal extracellular tags, no intracellular tags, and no function-abrogating positions are reported in the ledger. The EGFP fused at the C-terminus in the S6-p75NTR-EGFP construct is intracellular (C-terminus is cytoplasmic, residues 273–427) and is not proposed as a surface-tag site.
